chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, “May I be made your ransom, if a woman remains for ten days seeing blood, then she becomes pure and remains for three days in purity, then after that she sees blood, does she refrain from salat (prayer)?” He said, “No. This one is a mustaḥāḍah. She performs ghusl, inserts cotton, and combines two prayers with one ghusl, and her husband may approach her if he wishes.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: the blood seen, which determines the ruling of ḥayḍ or istiḥāḍah
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), whose obligation is being asked about
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman being asked about in the legal case
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا: her husband, whose marital access is addressed in the ruling
key_terms.طَهُرَتْ: she became pure from the earlier bleeding
key_terms.قُطْنَةً: cotton inserted as part of managing istiḥāḍah bleeding
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah rather than ḥayḍ

ai.seo_question: If a woman sees blood again after ten days of ḥayḍ and three days of purity, does she stop praying?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman who sees blood for ten days, then experiences three days of purity, and then sees blood again. The Imam عليه السلام rules that she is considered mustaḥāḍah, so she does not leave salat (prayer), but instead follows the rulings of istiḥāḍah including ghusl and the prescribed measures of ritual purity.
